p0.original: 第十一章 运用强制力避免伤害
p0.en: Chapter XI. Use of force to avoid harm

p1.original: 如果冲突的双方都能充分表达观察、感受、需要和请求，并得到对方的理解，那么，双方的需要通常可以同时得到满足。至少，他们可以求同存异。
p1.en: If both parties to the conflict are able to fully express their views, feelings, needs and requests and are understood by each other, then their needs can normally be met simultaneously. At least, they can try to live together.

p2.original: 然而，在有些时候，双方没有机会进行这样的对话。例如，有一方也许不想交流，或是危险迫在眉睫没有时间交流。在这样的情况下，我们可能就需要使用强制力来避免伤害。
p2.en: However, in some cases, the parties did not have the opportunity to engage in such a dialogue. For example, one party may not want to communicate, or there is no time available for communication in the imminent danger. In such cases, we may need to use force to avoid harm.

p4.original: 需要注意的是，在非暴力沟通中，我们运用强制力是出于防卫的目的而不是为了惩罚对方。例如，我们抱住年幼的孩子不让他跑到公路上，那是为了他的安全。如果我们打孩子的屁股或骂他：“你怎么这么笨！”那么，我们就是在惩罚他。
p4.en: It needs to be noted that in Nonviolent Communication, we use coercion for defensive purposes, not for the purpose of punishing the other. For example, we held young children away from the road for his safety. If we hit the kid's ass or yell at him, "You're so stupid! So, we're punishing him.

p5.original: 在使用防卫性的强制力时，我们把注意力放在了自己和他人的需要上，而不评价对方及其行为。我们不会去指责一个要跑到公路上的孩子；我们只是想保护他。非暴力沟通认为，如果一个人做的事情会伤害到自己或他人，那是因为他不够成熟。为此，他需要得到帮助。如果我们不够成熟，我们可能会有以下的表现：（1）我们意识不到自己行为的后果；（2）我们认识不到，我们并不需要通过惩罚他人来满足自己的需要；（3）我们相信，我们有“权利”去惩罚或伤害他人，因为他们是罪有应得；（4）我们产生了幻觉，例如，听到“某种声音”叫我们去杀人。
p5.en: In using defensive force, we focus on our own needs and those of others, without evaluating each other and their behaviour. We don't blame a kid who's on the road. We're just trying to protect him. Nonviolent Communication is based on the belief that a person is not mature enough to do something that harms himself or others. He needs help for that. If we are not mature enough, we may have the following: (1) We are unaware of the consequences of our actions; (2) We do not recognize that we do not need to meet our needs by punishing others; (3) We believe that we have a “right” to punish or harm others because they deserve it; (4) We are hallucinating, for example, to hear “some kind of voice” calling us to kill.

p6.original: 相反，在使用惩罚性的强制力时，我们认为某些人是邪恶的，为了让他们悔改，必须给他们一点颜色看看。此时，我们希望痛苦能让他们：（1）意识到自己的过错；（2）感到懊悔；（3）改变行为。然而，在实际生活中，惩罚往往加强了对方的敌意和抵触心理，使双方的关系更加疏远。
p6.en: On the contrary, when punitive force is used, we believe that some people are evil and that in order for them to repent, they must be given a little colour. At this point, we hope that pain will make them (1) aware of their own faults; (2) Regret; (3) Change of behaviour. In practice, however, punishment tends to reinforce the hostility and resistance of the other and further alienate the relationship between the parties.

p8.original: 体罚是常见的惩罚方式。我发现，家长对此有截然不同的看法。有些家长相信，通过体罚，例如打屁股，可以让孩子清楚地知道不该做什么。另外一些家长则坚决反对这种做法，他们认为，体罚会让孩子形成这样的认识：当别的方法都不起作用时，就可以用武力来解决问题。
p8.en: Corporal punishment is a common form of punishment. I found that parents have a very different view of this. Some parents believe that through corporal punishment, such as as ass spanking, children can be well informed about what they should not do. Other parents were strongly opposed to the practice, and believed that corporal punishment would create an awareness among the child that force could be used to solve the problem when other methods did not work.

p9.original: 我的担心是，对体罚的恐惧会让孩子难以体会到父母的爱。经常有家长和我说，打骂孩子是不得已的事，因为他们没有其他办法能让孩子做“对他们有益的事情”。为了说明打骂确实管用，他们还提到了，有些孩子在事后很感激他们的父母。我养育了四个孩子，我深深地理解为人父母的难处。然而，我并不认为体罚孩子是教育孩子的好办法。
p9.en: My fear is that fear of corporal punishment can make it difficult for children to feel the love of their parents. Parents often told me that it was a last resort to abuse children because they had no other way of letting them do “what is good for them”. To illustrate the usefulness of the abuse, they also mentioned that some children were subsequently grateful to their parents. I raised four children, and I understood deeply the difficulty of being a parent. However, I do not think that corporal punishment of children is a good way to educate children.

p10.original: 首先，无数的例子表明了，有的时候孩子拒绝做一件对他们有益的事情，只是因为他们不想在父母的压力面前屈服。其次，即使体罚能带来立竿见影的效果，这也并不意味着，其他方法无法达到同样的效果。最后，我还担心，体罚孩子会造成不良的社会影响。如果我们把暴力作为解决问题的办法，虽然孩子可能会去做我们要求的事，但这样做难道不是在鼓励孩子用暴力来解决冲突吗？
p10.en: First, countless examples show that sometimes children refuse to do something that is good for them, simply because they do not want to give in to the pressure of their parents. Second, even if corporal punishment had immediate effects, that did not mean that other methods could not achieve the same effect. Finally, I am also concerned about the negative social impact of corporal punishment of children. If we use violence as a solution to the problem, and while children may do what we ask, isn't that encouraging children to use violence to resolve conflicts?

p11.original: 除了体罚外，指责或否定他人也是常见的惩罚方式。例如，如果孩子没有照家长的话去做，父母可能就会说他“自私”“不尊重父母”等等。另外一种惩罚方式是不给孩子某种好处，例如不给零花钱。在这种情形中，变得冷漠是一种强有力的威胁。
p11.en: In addition to corporal punishment, it is common to accuse or deny others. For example, if the child does not do what the parents say, the parents may say he is “selfish” “not respectful of the parents”. Another form of punishment is the failure to give the child some benefit, such as the non-payment of petty money. In such a situation, indifference is a powerful threat.

p13.original: 当我们为了回避惩罚去做事情时，我们可能会忽视事情本身的价值，而陷于对失败的忧虑。如果员工的表现只是在服从管理层的命令，士气就会受到影响；或迟或早，工作效率就会降低。如果孩子刷牙是因为担心受到批评或被嘲笑，他们的口腔健康可能会得以改善，但自尊却会受损。此外，我们都知道，惩罚将导致关系的疏远。一旦我们被看作是施暴的人，我们就很难得到友善的回应。
p13.en: When we do things to avoid punishment, we may lose sight of the value of the matter itself and be caught in a fear of failure. Morals are affected if the performance of the staff is simply subject to management's orders; The efficiency of the work is reduced either later or earlier. If children brush their teeth for fear of criticism or ridicule, their oral health may be improved, but their self-esteem may be impaired. Moreover, we all know that punishment leads to alienation of relations. Once we are seen as perpetrators of violence, it is very difficult for us to get a friendly response.

p14.original: 有一次，我去一位朋友的单位拜访他。他是一所学校的校长。在谈话时，他透过办公室的玻璃看到有个学生在操场打人。他和我说了一句“对不起”，然后就冲了出去。他抓住了那个学生，重重地推了他一下，训斥道：“看你以后还敢不敢打比你小的同学！”校长回来后，我和他说：“我不认为你达到了目的。在我看来，他学到的是，在打比他弱小的人时，要注意附近是否有比他强壮的人，例如校长。而且，我认为，你的做法甚至还会强化他通过打架来解决问题的意识。”
p14.en: One time I went to a friend's office to visit him. He's the headmaster of a school. During the conversation, he saw a student beating someone in the playground through the glass of his office. He said, "I'm sorry," and then he went out. He grabbed the student, pushed him so hard, he said, "Look how dare you beat a fellow younger than you!" When the principal came back, I said, "I don't think you've achieved your goal. It seems to me that he has learned that when hitting someone smaller than him, care is to be taken of the presence of someone stronger than him, such as the headmaster. And, I think, your approach would even strengthen his sense of fighting to solve problems. I'm sorry.

p15.original: 在上述的情形下，我主张先倾听那个学生的感受和需要。例如，如果那个孩子动手打了叫他外号的同学，我可能会和他说：“看起来，你很生气，因为你希望得到尊重。”如果他肯定了这一点，我会接着表达我的感受、需要和请求，而不带有任何的指责：“我很伤心，因为我希望我们既能得到尊重，又不树敌。不知道你是否愿意和我一起探讨，是否有其他的方式可以使我们得到尊重？”
p15.en: In these circumstances, I would prefer to listen first to the feelings and needs of that student. For example, if that kid had hit his classmates, I might have said, "Look, you're angry because you want to be respected. “If he confirms this, I will continue to express my feelings, needs and requests without any accusations: “I am sad because I hope that we are both respected and unenemy. I wonder if you would like to explore with me if there are other ways to make us respect each other?

p17.original: 有两个问题可以帮助我们认识惩罚的局限性。第一个问题是，如果我不喜欢他现在的行为，那我希望他怎么做？如果我们只问这个问题，惩罚可能是有效果的，因为威胁或惩罚可以对他人的行为产生影响。然而，通过第二个问题，我们就可以清楚地看到惩罚的局限性：我希望他基于怎样的原因去做我想要他做的事情？
p17.en: There are two issues that can help us understand the limits of punishment. The first question is, if I don't like what he's doing now, what do I want him to do? If we only ask this question, the punishment may be effective, because the threat or punishment can have an impact on the behaviour of others. However, through the second question, we can see clearly the limits of punishment: I want him to do what I want him to do for what reasons?

p18.original: 我们很少提及第二个问题，借助这个问题，我们可以发现惩罚或奖励很难实现我们的目的。例如，如果我们希望孩子出于爱干净或对父母的关心去打扫房间，指责或威胁显然不太可能起到积极的作用。常见的情形是，孩子打扫房间是为了服从父母的指示（“因为妈妈是这样吩咐的”）——他们也许是为了得到父母的疼爱或避免受到惩罚。我相信，了解别人基于什么样的原因来满足我们的愿望是至关重要的。在非暴力沟通中，我们看重每个人选择生活的自由。与此同时，非暴力沟通还强调，我们彼此相互依存，我们的幸福与他人的幸福息息相关。
p18.en: We rarely mention the second issue, by which we can find that punishment or rewards are difficult to achieve. For example, if we want children to clean their rooms out of love or concern for their parents, accusations or threats are clearly unlikely to play a positive role. It is common for children to clean their rooms in order to comply with their parents' instructions (“because this is what their mother told them”) - perhaps in order to get the love of their parents or avoid punishment. I am convinced that it is essential to understand what reasons others have to meet our aspirations. In Nonviolent Communication, we value everyone's freedom to choose life. At the same time, Nonviolent Communication also emphasizes that we are interdependent and that our happiness is closely linked to the well-being of others.

p19.original: 运用非暴力沟通来重建校园秩序
p19.en: Using Nonviolent Communication to re-establish school order

p20.original: 现在，我想谈谈我们与一些学生在一所学校中重建校园秩序的经历。这所学校接纳的是在其他学校学不下去或被勒令退学的学生。学校的管理人员希望，通过在校园中普及非暴力沟通，学校可以与这些学生形成良好的互动。我的工作是培训教师队伍，并担任顾问一年。由于只有四天时间来培训教师，我没有解释清楚非暴力沟通与放任不管之间的区别。因此，在出现矛盾和冲突的时候，有些教师选择了回避，而不积极地介入。这样，校园秩序更加混乱，以致学校管理层开始考虑关闭学校。
p20.en: Now, I would like to talk about our experience with some students in re-establishing order in a school. This school accommodates students who cannot continue to study in other schools or who are ordered to drop out of school. School managers hope that schools will have good interaction with these students by promoting Nonviolent Communication in schools. My job is to train teachers and serve as a consultant for a year. Since there is only four days to train teachers, I have not explained the distinction between Nonviolent Communication and neglect. As a result, in the event of contradictions and conflicts, some teachers choose to eschew rather than engage actively. As a result, the school order became more disordered and school management began to consider closing schools.

p21.original: 此时，我告诉校方，我想和混乱中表现特别活跃的学生交流。于是，校长挑选了八个学生，他们的年龄在11岁至14岁之间。下面是我们会谈的摘录。
p21.en: At this point, I told the school that I wanted to communicate with students who were particularly active in the chaos. As a result, the headmaster selected eight students between the ages of 11 and 14. The following is an extract from our meeting.

p22.original: 马歇尔：（表达感受和需要，而不追根究底）“听到老师们说，许多班级的教学工作已无法正常进行，我很不安。我希望学校能够继续下去。所以，我想请你们帮助我了解现在学校中存在的问题以及你们的建议。”
p22.en: Marshall (expressing feelings and needs without looking) “I was disturbed to hear teachers say that teaching in many classes is no longer normal. I hope the school will continue. So I would like to ask you to help me understand the problems in schools and your suggestions.

p23.original: 学生甲：“这个学校的老师笨死了！”
p23.en: Student A: “The teacher of this school is stupid!

p24.original: 马歇尔：“你对他们的行为感到不满吗？”
p24.en: Marshall: Are you dissatisfied with their actions?

p25.original: 学生甲：“他们傻乎乎的，站在那里，什么都不做。”
p25.en: Student one: "They're stupid, standing there, doing nothing."

p26.original: 马歇尔：“在出现问题时，你希望他们能有所作为？”（继续了解他的感受和愿望）
p26.en: Marshall: “Do you want them to make a difference when a problem arises? Keep learning how he feels and wants

p27.original: 学生甲：“是这样的。不管别人做什么，他们只是面带微笑站在那里，真是一群白痴。”
p27.en: Student one: "This is it. No matter what people do, they just stand there smiling. What a bunch of idiots.

p28.original: 马歇尔：“给我举个例子好吗？”
p28.en: Marshall: "Can you give me an example?

p29.original: 学生甲：“这很容易。今天早上，有个家伙带着一瓶啤酒走进教室，所有人都看见了，但那位老师却装作什么也没发生。”
p29.en: Student one: "It's easy. This morning, a guy walked into the classroom with a bottle of beer and everyone saw it, but the teacher pretended nothing had happened.

p30.original: 马歇尔：“听起来，你看不起那位什么也不做的老师，你希望她采取行动。”（寻求反馈，看自己理解的是否准确）
p30.en: Marshall: “You don't look at the teacher who doesn't do anything. You want her to do something. ) (See if you understand correctly)

p32.original: 马歇尔：“我有些失望。看起来，我没能和老师们讲清楚我的意思。我希望，老师能和学生一起采取行动，重建学校的秩序。”
p32.en: Marshall: "I'm a little disappointed. Looks like I couldn't tell the teachers what I meant. I hope that teachers will take action with students to re-establish order in schools.

p33.original: （接着，讨论转向了一个急需解决的问题：一些学生在不想学习时会干扰到其他学生。）
p33.en: (The discussion then turned to an issue that needed to be addressed urgently: some students interfered with others when they did not want to study. I don't think so.

p34.original: 马歇尔：“我特别希望这个问题能够得到解决。因为老师们告诉我，这是他们最头痛的问题。怎么解决这个问题，我很想得到你们的建议。”
p34.en: Marshall: “I particularly hope that this problem will be resolved. Because the teachers told me it was their worst headache. I'd love to get your advice on how to fix this.

p35.original: 学生乙：“老师应该带根棍子来上班。”
p35.en: Student B: “The teacher should bring a stick to work.

p36.original: 马歇尔：“你的意思说，如果有人打扰别的同学，老师就给他一棍子？”
p36.en: Marshall: "You mean if someone bothers someone else, the teacher gives him a stick?

p37.original: 学生乙：“我想这是解决问题的唯一办法。”
p37.en: Student B: I think it's the only way to solve this problem.

p38.original: 马歇尔：“你不相信有其他的解决办法？”（继续了解这位学生的感受）
p38.en: Marshall: "You don't believe in other solutions? Keep learning how this student feels

p40.original: 马歇尔：“如果这是唯一的方式，我会很沮丧。我希望我们能找到别的解决办法。”
p40.en: "If it's the only way, I'll be very upset. I hope we find another solution.

p42.original: 马歇尔：“有几个原因。例如，在回家时，有三四个被我用棍子打过的人围住我，那怎么办？”
p42.en: Marshall: "There are several reasons. For example, when I come home, three or four people I've been beaten with sticks are rounding me up. What do we do?

p43.original: 学生乙：（笑）“那你最好带根大点的棍子。”
p43.en: Student B: "Then you better bring a bigger stick.

p44.original: 马歇尔：（确信双方已相互理解，我继续说）“你知道，用这样的方式来处理事情，我会遇到麻烦的。我不会每一次都记得带根大棍子，即使我能记得，我也不想用它来打任何人。”
p44.en: Marshall: “Be sure that the two sides understand each other, I will continue to say: “You know, I'll be in trouble when things are handled in this way. I don't remember a big stick every time, even if I can remember, and I don't want to hit anybody with it.

p45.original: 学生乙：“那你们可以把那些捣蛋鬼开除。”
p45.en: Student B: "Then you can fire the troublemakers.

p46.original: 马歇尔：“如果一定要这样做，我也会很沮丧。我希望有别的方式来解决冲突，而不用把任何一位同学开除。”
p46.en: Marshall: If I had to do this, I would have been frustrated. I hope that there will be another way to resolve the conflict without firing any of our fellow students.

p47.original: 学生甲：“如果有谁不想学习，你不妨让他去一个没有人学习的教室呆着？”
p47.en: Student A: “If anyone wants to study, you can let him go to a classroom where no one will study?

p48.original: 马歇尔：“你是说，我们腾出一间教室，让不想学习的人有个去处，是吗？”
p48.en: Marshall: "You mean, we're gonna make room for people who don't want to learn, right?

p49.original: 学生甲：“是的。如果他们不想学习，呆在班级里，也没什么用。”
p49.en: Student one: "Yes. If they don't want to study, it won't help if they stay in class.

p50.original: 马歇尔：“对这个想法，我很感兴趣。具体怎么操作呢？”
p50.en: Marshall: I'm interested in this idea. How does it work?

p51.original: 学生甲：“有的时候，你来学校上学，但心情很不好，你什么都不想做，这时，你就可以先去那个教室。等你想学习了，再回到班级中。”
p51.en: Student one: “Sometimes you come to school, but you're in a bad mood, you don't want to do anything, and then you can go to that classroom first. When you're ready to study, go back to class.

p52.original: 马歇尔：“我明白你的意思了。不过，老师们可能会担心，同学们是否会自愿去那个教室。”
p52.en: Marshall: I see what you mean. However, teachers may be concerned about whether they will volunteer to go to that classroom.

p53.original: 学生甲：（自信地说）“他们会去的。”

p54.original: 我和校方说，这样做不是为了惩罚任何人，而是给暂时不想学习的学生提供一个去处，并给那些愿意学习的学生创造条件。我相信，如果学生能够明白这一点，这样做是很有用的。我还提醒校方，如果学生知道这个措施是一些学生集体讨论的结果，而不是校方的命令，那么，他们将更愿意配合。
p54.en: I and the school said that this was not about punishing anyone, but rather about providing a place for students who were temporarily unwilling to study and creating conditions for those who were willing to study. I believe that it would be useful if students understood that. I also reminded the school community that if the students knew that the measure was the result of a collective discussion among some students and not of an order from the school, they would be more willing to cooperate.

p55.original: 于是，学校就设置了一个教室，来到这个教室的学生，可以什么都不做。有时，有的学生主动提出到这个教室去；在另外一些时候，如果某个学生的行为妨碍了别人的学习，老师也会请他去。在这个教室中，我们安排了一位熟练掌握非暴力沟通的教师，当学生进来时，她会主动和他们交谈。这个教室的设置对学校秩序的恢复起到了极为重要的影响。因为那些曾参加讨论的学生告诉他们的同学：这样做是为了保护各位同学的学习权利。我们也借这件事向教师们说明了，除了回避矛盾以及实施惩罚，我们还可以通过别的办法来解决问题。
p55.en: As a result, a classroom was set up in the school, where students could do nothing. In some cases, students offered to go to this classroom; At other times, if the behaviour of a student prevents others from learning, the teacher invites him to attend. In this classroom, we have a teacher who is skilled in Nonviolent Communication, and when the students come in, she talks to them on her own initiative. The establishment of this classroom has had an extremely important impact on the restoration of school order. Because the students who participated in the discussion told their classmates that they were doing so to protect their right to study. We have also made it clear to teachers that, in addition to avoiding contradictions and imposing penalties, we can solve problems by other means.

p57.original: 在有些情形中，我们没有机会和他人交流，这时，我们也许需要使用强制力来保护自己和他人。我们这样做，是为了避免伤害，而不是为了惩罚他人。如果我们威胁他人或实施惩罚，人们常常会产生敌意和抵触心理。这样，彼此的关系将会疏远。同时，惩罚还可能使人忽视事情本身的意义，而把注意力放在不服从的后果上。如果我们试图通过惩罚来使人们认识自己的需要，那么，我们很可能适得其反。
p57.en: In some cases, we do not have the opportunity to communicate with others, and at this point we may need to use force to protect ourselves and others. We do so to avoid harm, not to punish others. If we threaten others or punish them, people often generate hostility and resistance. In this way, the relationship will be alienated. At the same time, punishment may lead to neglect of the meaning of the matter itself and focus on the consequences of non-compliance. If we try to make people aware of their needs through punishment, then we are likely to be counterproductive.
